prompts.A: Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. WHOLE-GAME GRAPHIC LANGUAGE A — LIVING VIETNAMESE-INSPIRED LACQUER. Audacious, mature and graphic. Deep polished BLACK lacquer as spacious negative space; mineral VERMILION forms, thin irregular GOLD LEAF incisions, sparse warm EGGSHELL WHITE inlay. Not generic red-and-gold fantasy ornament: use asymmetric large masses, some deep bare black regions, finely controlled golden line accents. People are dignified expressive sharply designed silhouettes, slightly elongated angular body rhythm, simplified sculpted faces with eggshell cheek planes and dark eyes, clothing folds rendered by two or three lacquer color shapes and restrained engraved strokes. Full-body and dialogue portraits share exactly these shapes and facial rules. World: river is an almost-black lacquer mirror cut by a few gold contour ripples; houses and leaf shapes are powerful red/black masses with eggshell material accents, not photorealistic terrain. UI: black lacquer tablets with uneven red edges, crisp ivory readable type, thin gold structural strokes, red seal-like selected states; inventory icons are eggshell/gold inlay shapes on flat black slot grounds, dialogue portrait has the same lacquer/incised treatment. Lower sample strip also uses this material language without fake shiny gradients behind text. Shadow is graphic black rather than cinematic lighting. Bold, restrained, cohesive like an interactive artwork, not ornate all-over gold patterns. The design is fictional inspiration, not asserting lacquer existed in this depicted era. Create one WIDE 16:9 polished WHOLE-GAME VISUAL DIRECTION BOARD, not just an environment painting. The TOP TWO THIRDS is a believable full gameplay-screen mockup. In its scene a fictional ancient Vietnamese riverside community faces rising floodwater: an adult protagonist approaches a boatwright and a waiting family along a raised bamboo walkway, stilt houses, one loaded ferry, ordinary work and social choices. No combat spectacle. Include substantial readable UI integrated into the screen: top navigation with exact Vietnamese labels 'Thế giới', 'Cuộc đời', 'Túi đồ', 'Nhật ký'; a lower dialogue area with the boatwright's expressive portrait and short line 'Con nước lên rồi.' plus three clearly separated choices 'Hỏi chuyện', 'Giúp việc', 'Rời bến'. On the right, a compact inventory pane with six clear item icons (rope, clay jar, herb bundle, woven basket, grain sack, wood adze), not meaningless glyphs. BOTTOM THIRD is a crisp three-panel companion strip: LEFT two full-body adult character designs, the arriving person and older craftsperson, large enough to inspect proportions/clothing/face; CENTER three expressive portrait close-ups of distinct villagers; RIGHT a zoomed inventory/journal UI specimen with actual item slots, one selected state and one short journal entry, not a palette swatch. Thin separators, no oversized empty title zone. All elements—world, full-body people, portraits, items, interface shapes, icons and typography—MUST follow the single specified graphic language, not realistic characters pasted onto stylized scenery or generic modern UI. Both main scene and sample strip must be complete within edges. Vietnam-inspired simple bamboo/thatch/plain woven clothing as speculative game fiction, not archaeology or a religious artifact claim; no ornate pagoda tiles, torii, Chinese lantern rows, European medieval armor, giant gods, or weapon hotbar. No character customization or origin selection screen. This is an IMAGE-ONLY art-direction study, not real gameplay/model/engine output. Vietnamese UI text should be clean and legible; use few words, generous spacing, quiet text backgrounds. Do not imitate any existing game's proprietary UI. No watermarks or extra English labels.

prompts.C: Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. WHOLE-GAME GRAPHIC LANGUAGE C — LIVING INK, OFF-WHITE AND SCARLET. A bold expressive modern INK GRAPHIC RPG, dramatically different from a soft painted landscape. Almost monochrome: warm OFF-WHITE flat ground, dense BLACK pooled ink, occasional dry-brush grey edges; one SCARLET accent with precise roles for the protagonist cloth and selected UI choice. Strong mature character designs with large simple black hair masses, elegant asymmetric gestures, angular cloth silhouettes, eyes and brows readable with a few decisive marks; NOT chibi, not sketchy unfinished mannequins. Full-body designs and closeup dialogue portraits must clearly be drawn by same hand. The world alternates carved-looking black silhouettes with broad calm white paths and water, selective broken strokes on wet wood and reeds, no realistic color fill or painterly green foliage. A red thread-like stroke suggests a visual flow along the path as an ART MOTIF, not a canonical magic trail. UI is an integral drawn composition: clean off-white dialogue fields bounded by one heavy irregular black brush edge, black well-spaced Vietnamese type, scarlet square/underline selected states; sharp irregular paper-like menu tabs, hand-inked six-item silhouettes in an orderly grid; journal combines sparse text and small charcoal sketches. Typography must remain usable, not random calligraphy. Red should be very sparse so its design role reads immediately; no manga speed-line clutter, no gore or horror, no unrelated rainbow color. Strong negative space and graphic hierarchy let the screen feel like a living illustrated novel with real game navigation rather than a comic page pasted over generic scenery.
